He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] and [[California Baptist Lancers men's basketball|California Baptist Lancers]] before starting his professional career in the Czech Republic, where he won a championship with [[Basketball Nymburk]]. He debuted in the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) in 2022 and has played for the [[Brisbane Bullets]], [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] and [[Tasmania JackJumpers]]. ==Early life== Gak was born in [[Egypt]] to South Sudanese refugees, but his family soon decided to leave the country and move to [[Sydney]], [[New South Wales]].{{cite web|last=Tyler|first=Chris|url=https://www.espn.com.au/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22008613/australia-gorjok-gak-ready-make-impact-florida-gators|title=Gorjok Gak ready to make an impact for Florida Gators|work=ESPN.com.au|date=12 January 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427141332/https://www.espn.com.au/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22008613/australia-gorjok-gak-ready-make-impact-florida-gators|archive-date=27 April 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_42SOsvQBH4|title=One on One: Gorjok Gak & Jason Jitoboh|work=YouTube|publisher=[[Florida Gators]]|date=2 August 2019|access-date=28 April 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=555534443047266|title=From war-torn South Sudan to raising three of Australia's brightest young basketballing prospects, the Gak family has quite the story...|work=facebook.com/10NewsQLD|date=27 October 2022|access-date=27 April 2024}} He began playing basketball in Sydney and participated in the annual South Sudanese Australian National Classic. He attended [[St Augustine's College, Sydney|St Augustine's College]] before moving to the United States in 2014.{{cite web|last=Boyce|first=Dan|url=https://aussiehoopla.com/gorjok-gak-signs-florida-gators/|title=Florida Gators sign 6-foot-10 Sydney product Gorjok Gak|work=AussieHoopla.com|date=26 April 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240428025333/https://aussiehoopla.com/gorjok-gak-signs-florida-gators/|archive-date=28 April 2024}} His friend, [[Deng Adel]], convinced him to play high school basketball at Victory Rock Prep in [[Bradenton, Florida]]. Gak graduated from Victory Rock Prep in 2016 and averaged 13.9 points and 9.3 rebounds in his final season.{{cite career== Gak committed to [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] to play for [[Travis Ford]], but he was released from his letter-of-intent after Ford was fired at the end of the 2015–16 season.{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/victory-rock-center-gorjok-gak-gets-release-from-okahoma-state-letter-of-intent|title=Victory Rock center Gorjok Gak gets release from Oklahoma State letter of intent|work=[[USA Today]]|date=30 March April 2024}} Gak subsequently joined the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] in April 2016.{{cite web|url=https://floridagators.com/news/2016/4/26/mens-basketball-gators-add-gak-to-2016-class.aspx|title=Gators Add Gak to 2016 Class|work=[[Florida Gators]]|date=26 April 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240428022152/https://floridagators.com/news/2016/4/26/mens-basketball-gators-add-gak-to-2016-class.aspx|archive-date=28 April 2024}} Gak was initially ruled ineligible by the [[NCAA]] at the beginning of his rookie season, due to questions about the number of games he played at Victory Rock Prep.{{cite web|last=Brockway|first=Kevin|url=https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/2016/07/26/uf-basketball-freshman-gorjok-gak-ineligible/27429051007/|title=UF basketball freshman Gorjok Gak ineligible|work=[[The Gainesville Sun]]|date=26 July 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240428022559/https://www.gainesville.com/story/sports/college/2016/07/26/uf-basketball-freshman-gorjok-gak-ineligible/27429051007/|archive-date=28 April 2024}} His eligibility was restored in full following an appeal. As a freshman for Florida in [[2016–17 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2016–17]], Gak saw limited minutes and totaled 23 points and 23 rebounds in 15 appearances. As a sophomore in [[2017–18 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2017–18]], Gak battled through knee soreness and swelling all season and averaged 2.2 points and 2.4 rebounds in 29 games.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/gorjok-gak-1.html|title=Gorjok Gak|work=Sports-Reference.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427142814/https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/gorjok-gak-1.html|archive-date=27 April 2024}} Following off-season knee surgery, Gak [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] the [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2018–19 season]]. He returned to the Gators for the [[2019–20 Florida Gators men's basketball team|2019–20 season]] but suffered a dislocated shoulder in a practice in October.{{cite web|last=Goodall|first=Zach|url=https://www.si.com/college/florida/basketball/gators-center-gorjok-gak-transfers-california-baptist|title=Gators Center Gorjok Gak Transfers to California Baptist|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=FanNation|date=12 April 2020|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427143522/https://www.si.com/college/florida/basketball/gators-center-gorjok-gak-transfers-california-baptist|archive-date=27 April 2024}} He appeared in two games while battling various injuries before leaving the team at the end of December. In April 2020, Gak joined the [[California Baptist Lancers men's basketball|California Baptist Lancers]] as a graduate transfer. In the [[2020–21 California Baptist Lancers men's basketball team|2020–21 season]], Gak played and started in all 23 games and averaged 13.5 points and 10.3 rebounds per game. He scored in double figures 19 times and recorded 10 double-doubles. He scored a career-high 26 points against [[Long Beach State Beach men's basketball|Long Beach State]] on 23 January 2021. He was subsequently named All-[[Western Athletic Conference|WAC]] Second Team, WAC All-Defensive Team and WAC All-Newcomer Team. ==Professional career== In July 2021, Gak signed with [[Basketball Nymburk]] of the [[National Basketball League (Czech Republic)|Czech NBL]] for the 2021–22 season.{{cite web |last=Cross |first=Danny |date=23 July 2021 |title=Gak Signs Pro Contract With ERA Basketball Nymburk |url=https://cbulancers.com/news/2021/7/23/mens-basketball-gak-signs-pro-contract-with-era-basketball-nymburk.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427144208/https://cbulancers.com/news/2021/7/23/mens-basketball-gak-signs-pro-contract-with-era-basketball-nymburk.aspx |archive-date=27 April 2024 |work=[[California Baptist Lancers]]}} He helped the team win the Czech League championship and averaged 13.5 points, 10.1 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.7 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Gorjok-Gak/362991|title=Gorjok Gak|work=Australiabasket.com|access-date=27 April 2024|url-access=subscription}} On 6 July 2022, Gak signed with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) for the [[2022–23 NBL season|2022–23 season]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/gorjok-gak-signs-with-bullets|title=Gorjok Gak Signs with Bullets|work=NBL.com.au|date=6 July 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427144801/https://nbl.com.au/news/gorjok-gak-signs-with-bullets|archive-date=27 April 2024}} In round 13 against [[Melbourne United]], he recorded 18 points, 13 rebounds, three assists, two steals and a block.{{cite web|url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/phoenix-sign-211cm-centre-gorjok-gak-for-nbl24|title=Phoenix sign 211cm centre Gorjok Gak for NBL24|work=[[South East Melbourne Phoenix]]|date=10 April 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230410110653/https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/phoenix-sign-211cm-centre-gorjok-gak-for-nbl24|archive-date=10 April 2023|access-date=27 April 2024}} In 25 games, he averaged 4.6 points, 4.1 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. Gak joined the [[Willetton Tigers]] of the [[NBL1 West]] for the [[2023 NBL1 West season|2023 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.willettonbasketball.com.au/news/gorjok-gak-signed-for-the-zambrero-willetton-tigers-in-2023/|title=Gorjok Gak Signed for the Zambrero Willetton Tigers in 2023|work=WillettonBasketball.com.au|date=7 February 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240427145358/https://www.willettonbasketball.com.au/news/gorjok-gak-signed-for-the-zambrero-willetton-tigers-in-2023/|archive-date=27 April 2024}} He earned [[All-NBL1 West First Team]] honours and was named the league's Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://basketballwa.asn.au/2023-bwa-awards-night-nbl1-west-hall-of-fame-award-winners/|title=2023 BWA AWARDS NIGHT, NBL1 WEST & HALL OF FAME – AWARD WINNERS|work=BasketballWA.asn.au|date=23 July 2023|access-date=26 July 2023|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230726075755/https://basketballwa.asn.au/2023-bwa-awards-night-nbl1-west-hall-of-fame-award-winners/|archive-date=26 July 2023}} In 22 games, he averaged 20.1 points, 12.2 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game. On 10 April 2023, Gak signed with the [[South East Melbourne Phoenix]] for the [[2023–24 NBL season]]. He endured an injury-hit season, playing just 17 games and averaging 5.4 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/gak-signing-first-move-for-champions|title=Gak signing first move for champions|work=NBL.com.au|date=18 April 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240418081334/https://nbl.com.au/news/gak-signing-first-move-for-champions|archive-date=18 April 2024|access-date=27 April 2024}} Gak joined the [[Rockingham Flames]] for the [[2024 NBL1 West season]].{{cite web|url=https://nbl1.com.au/article/rockingham-add-defensive-superstar|title=Rockingham add Defensive superstar|work=NBL1.com.au|date=23 March 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919163629/https://nbl1.com.au/article/rockingham-add-defensive-superstar|archive-date=19 September 2024}} He was named to the All-NBL1 West First Team for the second straight season{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/NBLOneWest/posts/pfbid0sTF1SfTteFbrWU1TWXdGhTMt3XrNXnWmzucuPPrcLe2Rm8sK4rVku6jwpGfP3q17l|title=NBL1 West Men {{pipe}} All-NBL1 1st Team|work=facebook.com/NBLOneWest|date=20 July 2024|access-date=20 July 2024}} and earned [[NBL1 West All-Defensive Team]] honours.{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/NBLOneWest/posts/pfbid06UDB4keYhT9GFnpCTMJzSL6sVaKuEYBLTQCMjuj1VReyADUq7sctPg4A5UXQq94ql|title=The 2024 NBL1 West Men's All-Defensive Team|work=facebook.com/NBLOneWest|date=16 July 2024|access-date=16 July 2024}} In 20 games, he averaged 20.4 points, 10.95 rebounds, 2.25 assists and 1.2 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://nbl1.com.au/player-listing/gorjok-gak|title=Gorjok Gak|work=NBL1.com.au|access-date=19 September 2024}} On 18 April 2024, Gak signed a two-year deal with the [[Tasmania JackJumpers]], with the second year containing a club option. He played 24 games during [[2024–25 NBL season]], averaging 4 points per game.{{cite news |title=Tasmania JackJumpers decline team option on Gak contract |url=https://www.jackjumpers.com.au/news/thank-you-gorjok-gak |access-date=9 March 2025 |work=Tasmania JackJumpers |date=6 March 2025}} On 6 March 2025, the club chose to decline the second-year team option on his contract. On 22 March 2025, Gak signed with [[Peristeri B.C.|Peristeri]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] for the rest of the 2024–25 season.{{cite news |title=Ο Γκόρτζοκ Γκακ στο Περιστέρι Domino's • PERISTERI BC |url=https://www.peristeribc.gr/2025/03/22/%ce%bf-%ce%b3%ce%ba%cf%8c%cf%81%cf%84%ce%b6%ce%bf%ce%ba-%ce%b3%ce%ba%ce%b1%ce%ba-%cf%83%cf%84%ce%bf-%cf%80%ce%b5%cf%81%ce%b9%cf%83%cf%84%ce%ad%cf%81%ce%b9-dominos/ |access-date=22 March 2025 |work=peristeribc.gr |date=22 March 2025 |language=el}} In five games, he averaged 2.0 points and 1.0 rebounds per game. On 8 May 2025, Gak signed with the Casey Cavaliers of the [[NBL1 South]] for the rest of the [[2025 NBL1 season|2025 season]].{{cite news |title=NBL1 Player Announcement |url=https://www.facebook.com/CaseyBasketball/posts/pfbid0GyszVuvqH9LzfZrDKgfrxynuHc4Z8XfMMHXBRFGZExy8wwpfxp2JREFszDs4vgLxl |access-date=10 May 2025 |work=facebook.com/CaseyBasketball |date=8 May 2025}} In 13 games, he averaged 6.54 points, 3.54 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Gorjok Gak |url=https://nbl1.com.au/player-listing/gorjok-gak-c1d3de8b-cc5a-11ed-8076-0941e9b69ab1 |website=nbl1.com.au |access-date=19 August 2025}} On 17 May 2025, Gak signed with the South East Melbourne Phoenix for the [[2025–26 NBL season]], returning to the team for a second stint.{{cite news |title=Return to the Heartland: Gak runs it back at Phoenix |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/return-to-the-heartland-gak-runs-it-back-at-phoenix |access-date=17 May 2025 |work=nbl.com.au |date=17 May 2025 |language=en}} On 18 December, Gak was released by the Phoenix so he could pursue opportunities overseas.{{cite web |title=Gorjok Gak departs Phoenix |url=https://www.semphoenix.com.au/news/gorjok-gak-departs-phoenix |website=South East Melbourne Phoenix |access-date=18 December 2025 |date=18 December 2025}} On 22 December 2025, Gak signed with the [[Sichuan Blue Whales]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] for the rest of the 2025–26 season.{{cite web |title=结束全华班，官方：四川男篮签下澳大利亚中锋戈尔乔克-加克 |url=https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20251222A02M5800 |website=news.qq.com |access-date=18 January 2026 |date=22 December 2025}} In July 2026, Gak joined the [[Niagara River Lions]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]] (CEBL) for the rest of the [[2026 CEBL season|2026 season]].{{cite news |title=RIVER LIONS SIGN AUSTRALIAN CENTER GORJOK GAK |url=https://www.riverlions.ca/river-lions-sign-australian-center-gorjok-gak |access-date=25 August 2026 |work=riverlions.ca |date=9 July 2026}} ==National team== Gak played for the [[Australia at the 2017 Summer Universiade#Basketball|Australian University National Team]] in 2017 at the [[Basketball at the 2017 Summer Universiade – Men's tournament|World University Games]] in Taipei. In eight games, he averaged 11.1 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game. ==Personal life== Gak is the son of Ajok Langar and Matur Gak and his siblings are Deng, Nyapath, [[Akoldah Gak|Akoldah]], Adeng and Ayen.
